proposed_widenings.name: Attachment.item
proposed_widenings.justification: The activation targets and changes the carpet itself, not the wielder, a creature target, or an area. The current activation surface cannot attach phases to an item/object subject.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You can make this carpet hover and fly by taking a Magic action and using the carpet's command word. It moves according to your directions if you are within 30 feet of it.

proposed_widenings.name: MagicItem size/speed/capacity mode selection
proposed_widenings.justification: A single Carpet of Flying can exist in one of four GM-chosen size profiles with distinct capacity and Fly Speed values. The current magic-item surface has no honest way to encode one item record with closed variant profiles.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Four sizes of Carpet of Flying exist. The GM chooses the size of a given carpet or determines it randomly by rolling on the following table.

proposed_widenings.name: load-conditioned speed modifier
proposed_widenings.justification: The item's speed changes as a deterministic function of carried weight. The current surface has speed-setting atoms, but no way to express a persistent threshold rule like 'halve Fly Speed above normal capacity up to twice capacity.'
proposed_widenings.evidence: A carpet can carry up to twice the weight shown on the table, but its Fly Speed is halved if it carries more than its normal capacity.

notes: Stopped before authoring per protocol. `magic_item` is the correct top-level kind, but the existing authored surface cannot honestly represent an independently moving item with GM-chosen size variants and load-based speed changes.
